import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import os
import lightgbm as lgb
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
from datetime import datetime
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Paths
train_path = "./input/labels.csv"
test_path = "./input/test.csv"
sample_submission_path = "./input/sample_submission.csv"
submission_path = "./submission/submission.csv"

# Create submission directory if needed
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

# Load data
print("Loading data...")
train = pd.read_csv(train_path)
test = pd.read_csv(test_path)
sample_submission = pd.read_csv(sample_submission_path)

print(f"Train shape: {train.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test.shape}")

# Handle missing values and outliers
print("Cleaning data...")
train["pickup_datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(train["pickup_datetime"])
test["pickup_datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(test["pickup_datetime"])

# Clip coordinates to realistic NYC bounds
train["pickup_latitude"] = train["pickup_latitude"].clip(40, 41)
train["pickup_longitude"] = train["pickup_longitude"].clip(-75, -73)
train["dropoff_latitude"] = train["dropoff_latitude"].clip(40, 41)
train["dropoff_longitude"] = train["dropoff_longitude"].clip(-75, -73)
test["pickup_latitude"] = test["pickup_latitude"].clip(40, 41)
test["pickup_longitude"] = test["pickup_longitude"].clip(-75, -73)
test["dropoff_latitude"] = test["dropoff_latitude"].clip(40, 41)
test["dropoff_longitude"] = test["dropoff_longitude"].clip(-75, -73)

# Drop extreme coordinate outliers
train = train.dropna(
    subset=[
        "pickup_latitude",
        "pickup_longitude",
        "dropoff_latitude",
        "dropoff_longitude",
    ]
)
test = test.dropna(
    subset=[
        "pickup_latitude",
        "pickup_longitude",
        "dropoff_latitude",
        "dropoff_longitude",
    ]
)

print(f"After cleaning - Train shape: {train.shape}")
print(f"After cleaning - Test shape: {test.shape}")

# Feature engineering with vectorized operations
print("Engineering features...")


# Haversine distance calculation using numpy
def calculate_distance_km(df):
    lats1 = np.radians(df["pickup_latitude"].values.astype(np.float64))
    lons1 = np.radians(df["pickup_longitude"].values.astype(np.float64))
    lats2 = np.radians(df["dropoff_latitude"].values.astype(np.float64))
    lons2 = np.radians(df["dropoff_longitude"].values.astype(np.float64))

    dlat = lats2 - lats1
    dlon = lons2 - lons1
    a = np.sin(dlat / 2) ** 2 + np.cos(lats1) * np.cos(lats2) * np.sin(dlon / 2) ** 2
    c = 2 * np.arctan2(np.sqrt(a), np.sqrt(1 - a))
    return 6371 * c


train["distance_km"] = calculate_distance_km(train)
test["distance_km"] = calculate_distance_km(test)

# Enhanced temporal features including month, day_of_month, and year
train["hour"] = train["pickup_datetime"].dt.hour
train["day_of_week"] = train["pickup_datetime"].dt.dayofweek
train["is_weekend"] = (train["day_of_week"] >= 5).astype(int)
train["is_rush_hour_morning"] = ((train["hour"] >= 6) & (train["hour"] <= 9)).astype(
    int
)
train["is_rush_hour_evening"] = ((train["hour"] >= 17) & (train["hour"] <= 19)).astype(
    int
)
train["month"] = train["pickup_datetime"].dt.month
train["day_of_month"] = train["pickup_datetime"].dt.day
train["year"] = train["pickup_datetime"].dt.year
train["quarter"] = (train["month"] - 1) // 3 + 1
train["is_peak_season"] = ((train["month"] >= 4) & (train["month"] <= 10)).astype(int)

test["hour"] = test["pickup_datetime"].dt.hour
test["day_of_week"] = test["pickup_datetime"].dt.dayofweek
test["is_weekend"] = (test["day_of_week"] >= 5).astype(int)
test["is_rush_hour_morning"] = ((test["hour"] >= 6) & (test["hour"] <= 9)).astype(int)
test["is_rush_hour_evening"] = ((test["hour"] >= 17) & (test["hour"] <= 19)).astype(int)
test["month"] = test["pickup_datetime"].dt.month
test["day_of_month"] = test["pickup_datetime"].dt.day
test["year"] = test["pickup_datetime"].dt.year
test["quarter"] = (test["month"] - 1) // 3 + 1
test["is_peak_season"] = ((test["month"] >= 4) & (test["month"] <= 10)).astype(int)

# Distance-based polynomial features
train["distance_sq"] = train["distance_km"] ** 2
train["distance_cubed"] = train["distance_km"] ** 3
test["distance_sq"] = test["distance_km"] ** 2
test["distance_cubed"] = test["distance_km"] ** 3

# Distance by passenger interaction
train["dist_passenger"] = train["distance_km"] * train["passenger_count"]
test["dist_passenger"] = test["distance_km"] * test["passenger_count"]

# NEW: Time-based distance interaction features to capture rush hour premium
# The model will learn different distance cost curves during peak hours
train["dist_rush_hour_morning"] = train["distance_km"] * train["is_rush_hour_morning"]
train["dist_rush_hour_evening"] = train["distance_km"] * train["is_rush_hour_evening"]
train["dist_weekend"] = train["distance_km"] * train["is_weekend"]
train["dist_rush_hour_morning_sq"] = (
    train["distance_km"] ** 2 * train["is_rush_hour_morning"]
)
train["dist_rush_hour_evening_sq"] = (
    train["distance_km"] ** 2 * train["is_rush_hour_evening"]
)

test["dist_rush_hour_morning"] = test["distance_km"] * test["is_rush_hour_morning"]
test["dist_rush_hour_evening"] = test["distance_km"] * test["is_rush_hour_evening"]
test["dist_weekend"] = test["distance_km"] * test["is_weekend"]
test["dist_rush_hour_morning_sq"] = (
    test["distance_km"] ** 2 * test["is_rush_hour_morning"]
)
test["dist_rush_hour_evening_sq"] = (
    test["distance_km"] ** 2 * test["is_rush_hour_evening"]
)

# Feature columns (includes new interaction features)
feature_cols = [
    "pickup_latitude",
    "pickup_longitude",
    "dropoff_latitude",
    "dropoff_longitude",
    "distance_km",
    "distance_sq",
    "distance_cubed",
    "passenger_count",
    "dist_passenger",
    "hour",
    "day_of_week",
    "is_weekend",
    "is_rush_hour_morning",
    "is_rush_hour_evening",
    "month",
    "day_of_month",
    "year",
    "quarter",
    "is_peak_season",
    "dist_rush_hour_morning",  # NEW
    "dist_rush_hour_evening",  # NEW
    "dist_weekend",  # NEW
    "dist_rush_hour_morning_sq",  # NEW
    "dist_rush_hour_evening_sq",  # NEW
]

# Use larger stratified sample for better distribution preservation
print("Creating stratified sample (300K rows)...")
n_samples = min(300000, len(train))
fare_quartiles = np.percentile(train["fare_amount"], [25, 50, 75])
fare_quartiles = [
    0,
    fare_quartiles[0],
    fare_quartiles[1],
    fare_quartiles[2],
    float("inf"),
]
train["fare_bin"] = pd.cut(train["fare_amount"], bins=fare_quartiles, labels=False)

# Sample from each fare quantile
samples_per_quantile = n_samples // 5
stratified_samples = []
for i in range(5):
    subset = train[train["fare_bin"] == i]
    stratified_samples.append(
        subset.sample(n=min(samples_per_quantile, len(subset)), random_state=42)
    )

train_sampled = pd.concat(stratified_samples, ignore_index=True)
train_sampled = train_sampled.drop("fare_bin", axis=1)

print(f"Stratified sample size: {len(train_sampled)}")

# Prepare training data
print("Preparing training data...")
X_train = train_sampled[feature_cols].fillna(-1).astype(float)
y_train = train_sampled["fare_amount"]

# Hold out validation set (never retrained on full data)
print("Splitting for validation...")
X_train_small, X_val, y_train_small, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_train, y_train, test_size=0.2, random_state=42
)

# Combine remaining for test hold-out
X_test_full = pd.concat([X_train_small, X_train]).reset_index(drop=True)
y_test_full = pd.concat([y_train_small, y_train]).reset_index(drop=True)

print(
    f"Training set: {len(X_train_small)}, Validation: {len(X_val)}, Full holdout test: {len(X_test_full)}"
)

# Train LightGBM model with optimized parameters
print("Training LightGBM Regressor...")
train_data = lgb.Dataset(X_train_small, label=y_train_small)
val_data = lgb.Dataset(X_val, label=y_val, reference=train_data)

params = {
    "objective": "regression",
    "metric": "rmse",
    "boosting_type": "gbdt",
    "num_leaves": 63,
    "learning_rate": 0.05,
    "feature_fraction": 0.8,
    "bagging_fraction": 0.8,
    "bagging_freq": 5,
    "verbose": -1,
    "n_jobs": 4,
}

model = lgb.train(
    params,
    train_data,
    num_boost_round=500,
    valid_sets=[val_data],
    valid_names=["valid"],
    callbacks=[lgb.early_stopping(stopping_rounds=50, verbose=False)],
)

# Validate on held-out set
print("Evaluating on validation set...")
y_val_pred = model.predict(X_val, num_iteration=model.best_iteration)
rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_val, y_val_pred))
print(f"Validation RMSE: {rmse:.4f}")

# Prepare test predictions
print("Generating test predictions...")
X_test = test[feature_cols].fillna(-1).astype(float)
test_predictions = model.predict(X_test, num_iteration=model.best_iteration)

# Create submission matching sample format
submission = pd.DataFrame(
    {"key": test["key"], "fare_amount": test_predictions.round(2)}
)
submission.to_csv(submission_path, index=False)

print(f"\nSubmission saved to {submission_path}")
print(f"RMSE computed on validation set: {round(rmse, 4)}")
print("Done!")
plan: I will improve the solution by adding interaction features between distance and rush hour indicators to capture time-of-day fare multipliers. The previous solution had separate temporal and distance features but didn't combine them to model how fares vary by distance during peak hours. This atomic improvement adds three new interaction features (distance * morning rush hour, distance * evening rush hour, and distance * weekend) that capture the premium taxi pricing structure during high-demand periods. This complements the existing temporal features without requiring architectural changes or excessive memory.
